claims.text: Role in Sjögren: dry mouth: cevimeline 30 mg PO 3 times a day (or pilocarpine 5 mg) can stimulate saliva;
claims.quote: Oral pilocarpine 5 mg 3 times a day or oral cevimeline hydrochloride 30 mg 3 times a day can stimulate salivary production but should be avoided in patients with bronchospasm and closed-angle glaucoma.

claims.text: avoid w bronchospasm or closed-angle glaucoma.
claims.quote: should be avoided in patients with bronchospasm and closed-angle glaucoma

claims.text: Cevimeline (Evoxac) dose, dry mouth in Sjögren's syndrome: 30 mg taken three times a day; insufficient safety information to support doses greater than 30 mg tid.
claims.quote: The recommended dose of cevimeline hydrochloride capsules is 30 mg taken three times a day. There is insufficient safety information to support doses greater than 30 mg tid.

claims.text: Cevimeline (Evoxac) CI: uncontrolled asthma, known hypersensitivity to cevimeline, and when miosis is undesirable, e.g., acute iritis and narrow-angle (angle-closure) glaucoma.
claims.quote: Cevimeline is contraindicated in patients with uncontrolled asthma, known hypersensitivity to cevimeline, and when miosis is undesirable, e.g., in acute iritis and in narrow-angle (angle-closure) glaucoma.

claims.text: Cevimeline (Evoxac) cardiovascular: Can potentially alter cardiac conduction and/or HR; pts w significant cardiovascular dz may be unable to compensate for transient changes in hemodynamics or rhythm; use w caution and under close medical supervision in pts w Hx of cardiovascular dz evidenced by angina pectoris or myocardial infarction.
claims.quote: Cevimeline can potentially alter cardiac conduction and/or heart rate. Patients with significant cardiovascular disease may potentially be unable to compensate for transient changes in hemodynamics or rhythm induced by EVOXAC ®. EVOXAC ® should be used with caution and under close medical supervision in patients with a history of cardiovascular disease evidenced by angina pectoris or myocardial infarction.

claims.text: Cevimeline (Evoxac) pulmonary: Can potentially ↑ airway resistance, bronchial smooth muscle tone, and bronchial secretions; administer w caution and w close medical supervision to pts w controlled asthma, chronic bronchitis, or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
claims.quote: Cevimeline can potentially increase airway resistance, bronchial smooth muscle tone, and bronchial secretions. Cevimeline should be administered with caution and with close medical supervision to patients with controlled asthma, chronic bronchitis, or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.

claims.text: Cevimeline (Evoxac) ocular: Ophthalmic formulations of muscarinic agonists reported to cause visual blurring which may result in ↓ visual acuity, especially at night and in pts w central lens changes, and to cause impairment of depth perception; caution advised while driving at night or performing hazardous activities in reduced lighting.
claims.quote: Ophthalmic formulations of muscarinic agonists have been reported to cause visual blurring which may result in decreased visual acuity, especially at night and in patients with central lens changes, and to cause impairment of depth perception. Caution should be advised while driving at night or performing hazardous activities in reduced lighting.

claims.text: Cevimeline (Evoxac) CYP2D6/CYP3A3/4 interactions: Drugs which inhibit CYP2D6 and CYP3A3/4 also inhibit the metabolism of cevimeline; use w caution in pts known or suspected to be deficient in CYP2D6 activity, as they may be at ↑ risk of adverse events.
claims.quote: Drugs which inhibit CYP2D6 and CYP3A3/4 also inhibit the metabolism of cevimeline. Cevimeline should be used with caution in individuals known or suspected to be deficient in CYP2D6 activity, based on previous experience, as they may be at a higher risk of adverse events.

claims.text: Use w caution in pts taking beta adrenergic antagonists, because of the possibility of conduction disturbances.
claims.quote: Cevimeline should be administered with caution to patients taking beta adrenergic antagonists, because of the possibility of conduction disturbances.

claims.text: Cevimeline (Evoxac) OD signs: Toxicity = exaggerated parasympathomimetic effects: headache, visual disturbance, lacrimation, sweating, respiratory distress, gastrointestinal spasm, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, atrioventricular block, tachycardia, bradycardia, hypotension, hypertension, shock, mental confusion, cardiac arrhythmia, and tremors.
claims.quote: Cevimeline toxicity is characterized by an exaggeration of its parasympathomimetic effects. These may include: headache, visual disturbance, lacrimation, sweating, respiratory distress, gastrointestinal spasm, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, atrioventricular block, tachycardia, bradycardia, hypotension, hypertension, shock, mental confusion, cardiac arrhythmia, and tremors.

claims.text: Cevimeline (Evoxac) OD management: Manage as for other muscarinic agonists w general supportive measures; if medically indicated, atropine may be of value as an antidote for emergency use in pts who have had an OD; epinephrine may also be of value in severe cardiovascular depression or bronchoconstriction.
claims.quote: Management of the signs and symptoms of acute overdosage should be handled in a manner consistent with that indicated for other muscarinic agonists: general supportive measures should be instituted. If medically indicated, atropine, an anti-cholinergic agent, may be of value as an antidote for emergency use in patients who have had an overdose of cevimeline. If medically indicated, epinephrine may also be of value in the presence of severe cardiovascular depression or bronchoconstriction.
